Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. For the record, can you confirm you are the driver of the
vehicle involved in the collision in Pasadena, Texas?
A: Yes, that's right. I was driving my own car.
Q: Please walk me through what happened, starting from when you approached the intersection.
A: I was heading down the main road and wanted to turn left into a shopping center. I had my turn signal on and was
waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. When it looked clear, I started my turn, and then a vehicle coming the other way
hit the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you started to turn?
A: I saw hedalights further back, but it seemed far enough away. I misjudged how fast it was moving, and that's on
me, I suppose.
Q: What was the speed of your vehicle at the time of impact, as best you can estimate?
A: I was going slowly, maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour, since I was already in the turn.
Q: Did you have any injuries from the collision?
A: Yes. My neck snapped forward and back pretty hard. I've had stiffness and pain in my neck and upper back since
then, and I've had headaches most days.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment?
A: Yes, I was taken to an urgent care clinic the same day, and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week
since then. My doctor has me on muscle relaxers.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I've been unable to work my full schedule since the crash, and I want to make sure my medical bills are
covered.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
